items.stem: Why can simply deleting the protected attribute (e.g. race) fail to remove bias?

options.text: Other features can act as proxies that still encode the protected trait
options.rationale: Correct: correlated proxies reintroduce the bias.

options.text: Deleting a column always removes all bias
options.rationale: It does not, because of proxies.

options.text: The model cannot train without it
options.rationale: Models can train without it; that is not the issue.

options.text: It violates the licence of the dataset

items.explanation: Correct: correlated proxies reintroduce the bias.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about fairness metrics are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Demographic parity and equalised odds can be mathematically incompatible
options.rationale: Correct: you often cannot satisfy both at once.

options.text: Choosing a fairness definition is a context-dependent value judgement
options.rationale: Correct: the right metric depends on the harm and stakeholders.

options.text: One metric is objectively correct for all situations
options.rationale: No single metric fits every case.

options.text: Fairness metrics eliminate the need for human judgement

items.explanation: Correct: you often cannot satisfy both at once.

items.stem: What keeps a system fair after launch?

options.text: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review for drift and new harms
options.rationale: Correct: fairness can degrade as data and usage change.
One audit cannot cover future drift.
